title: Vue Router
description: Official router for Vue.js with nested routes and guards.

data.text: Vue Router is the official router for Vue.js. It integrates deeply with Vue's reactivity system and supports nested routes, route guards, and lazy loading.

data.title: Vue Router setup

data.text: Vue Router maps a path to a component and exposes the current route reactively. Named routes let you link by name rather than hard-coding paths, and `useRouter()` navigates from code. Route parameters are read with `useRoute()` or as props with `props: true`.

data.title: Named routes with parameters

data.text: A guard runs before a navigation is confirmed and can allow, redirect, or cancel it. This is where you enforce authentication, load data, or warn about unsaved changes. The `meta` field carries custom data such as `requiresAuth` that the guard reads.

data.title: An authentication guard
Interview angle: guard vs component check
data.text: Enforcing access in a navigation guard protects every route in one place, while checking inside the component runs after the component has already been created. Guards also run on the client, so they are a UX mechanism, not a security boundary — the server must still authorize the request. Saying both is the complete answer.

terms.definition: Hook that runs before route changes.
